payload.source_label: The two-equation acoustics system decomposes into two scalar waves moving in opposite directions

contract.statement: For the one-dimensional acoustic system p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + (1/ρ)p_x = 0 with constant material parameters, define c = √(K/ρ). The combinations w¹ = p + ρcu and w² = p − ρcu satisfy scalar transport equations with coefficients +c and −c, respectively (raw PDF page 24, equation (1.5) and displays following (1.6)). The source identifies this as a decomposition into two distinct acoustic waves traveling in opposite directions at the sound speed (raw PDF page 25, opening sentence). Precise regularity and parameter inequalities are implicit rather than formally enumerated in the displayed source.
assumptions: The fields satisfy p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + (1/ρ)p_x = 0 (raw PDF page 24, equation (1.5)).
The medium is one-dimensional and has constant K and ρ (raw PDF page 24, introduction to (1.5) and paragraph identifying the material constants).

The discussion uses a positive sound speed: the preceding one-way model explicitly has c > 0, and the two acoustic combinations are interpreted as distinct rightward and leftward waves. Separate inequalities K > 0 and ρ > 0 are not explicitly written on these pages (raw PDF page 24, introduction to (1.4) and acoustic transformation; raw PDF page 25, opening sentence).

Sufficient differentiability for the displayed first partial derivatives and their linear combinations is implicit in the assertion that the transformed fields satisfy the equations; no function space or weak-solution convention is supplied (raw PDF page 24, equation (1.5) and verification assertion following (1.6)).

The surrounding explanation places this acoustic decomposition within hyperbolic constant-coefficient systems, whose eigenvectors permit unique state decomposition and whose eigenvalues give wave speeds; the acoustic eigenvalues are −c and +c (raw PDF page 25, opening paragraph).
quantifiers: p(x,t) and u(x,t) are the two unknown fields, depending on one spatial coordinate x and time t; the passage does not specify their precise domains or explicitly state quantifiers (raw PDF page 24, equation (1.5) and its explanatory paragraph).

K and ρ are fixed material constants; c is defined from them by c = √(K/ρ), rather than introduced as an unrelated free parameter (raw PDF page 24, paragraph following (1.5) and definition following (1.6)).
